measure_note.polars_gpu: nvidia-smi device memory of the worker process, sampled during the timed action. cudf-polars allocates through an RMM async pool that keeps freed blocks (release threshold 90% of the device), so the value is the pool's high-water mark in that session so far, not the working set of the query: it did not fall in 28 of 32 sessions (see high_water_check) but fell in the other 4 (by up to 18.4 GiB; their samples reach 97% of the device), so there it is the pool size at the time of the action, and an upper bound on what the query needs only while the pool keeps its blocks
measure_note.spark_gpu: the largest device allocation a single task reported (RAPIDS task accumulator gpuMaxDeviceMemoryBytes, Spark event log) among the tasks launched inside the action; not a simultaneous total over concurrent tasks. The nvidia-smi samples (max_bytes, ...) are the RAPIDS pool reservation made at plugin start, not memory in use

gpu_memory.note: max_bytes / median_bytes / min_bytes are the nvidia-smi samples of the worker process tree during the timed action (worker peak_gpu_memory_bytes); maximum over the 3 measured trials, then over rounds; a sampled peak can miss short transients. What the sample means differs by engine: see measure / measure_note, and the task_reported blocks for Spark GPU

energy.definition: GPU board energy proxy = mean nvidia-smi power.draw over the session window x process wall time; CPU and host power are not included, and CPU-only engines show the idle GPU draw

meta.label: descriptive telemetry; not a pre-registered contrast; no causal claim
meta.definition: For each GPU engine, suite and scale: the nvidia-smi samples (utilization.gpu, utilization.memory, power.draw, clocks.current.sm) that fall inside the measured actions of the accepted rounds, pooled over queries, trials and rounds. idle_fraction is the share of samples with utilization.gpu below 10% (equal to the share of action wall time at uniform sampling). utilization.gpu is nvidia-smi's share of the sample period in which at least one kernel was executing, not SM occupancy. Descriptive; not a pre-registered contrast; no causal claim.
meta.power_limit_source: nvidia-smi -q, Current Power Limit of the first GPU
meta.resolution_note: nvidia-smi is sampled about every 200 ms, so an action of 1 s holds about 5 samples and the first and last sample of an action are partly outside it; actions shorter than 1 s (most SF1 actions) are left out of every statistic and counted in n_actions_excluded_short

meta.label: exploratory (post-hoc; not in the locked design §9)
meta.interval: Welch-type 95% interval on the log scale: the CPU times come from the side-study sessions and the GPU times from the main rounds, different sessions in different rounds, so the two sets of per-round values are unpaired (Welch-Satterthwaite df); no interval with fewer than two rounds on either side
meta.definition: time of the Polars CPU side-study sessions / time of the GPU side of the main rounds, per (suite, scale, query); above 1 means the GPU side was faster. The suite value is the same estimator over the per-round geometric mean of the queries timed in every round on both sides. This is post-hoc: not pre-registered, not part of the locked design (section 9), never mixed into C1-C4 or the crossover verdict.
meta.reason: no side study with two Polars versions

meta.label: exploratory (post-hoc; not in the locked design §9)
meta.denominator: best GPU engine per query and main round (polars_gpu or spark_gpu)
meta.interval: Welch-type 95% interval on the log scale: the CPU times come from the side-study sessions and the GPU times from the main rounds, different sessions in different rounds, so the two sets of per-round values are unpaired (Welch-Satterthwaite df); no interval with fewer than two rounds on either side
meta.definition: time of the Polars CPU side-study sessions / time of the GPU side of the main rounds, per (suite, scale, query); above 1 means the GPU side was faster. The suite value is the same estimator over the per-round geometric mean of the queries timed in every round on both sides. meta.reason: no side study with two Polars versions

meta.definition: time on A100 / time on H100 for the same GPU engine, query and scale; above 1 means the H100 host was faster. The A100 study is a single session per cell (no rounds), so the interval reflects the H100 round-to-round variation only. Hosts differ in GPU, vCPU count, RAM and software versions: not an equivalent comparison. The A100 side is the previous study's saved evidence (see study.label and study.differences), not the A100 campaign.
